summary.text: 视, the simplified form of 視, means ‘look at’ or ‘see.’ Its traditional form is analyzed as 見 ‘see’ plus 示 as a sound element, while early forms have also been interpreted as a picture of an eye above a standing person.

formation.text: The current character is identified as the simplified counterpart of 視. In the received traditional graph 視, the established dictionary analysis is phonosemantic: 見 contributes the meaning of seeing, and 示 supplies a phonetic cue. That analysis does not describe the distinct early pictographic form, which a paleographic interpretation reads as an eye above a standing figure.

components.text: The visible form 视 is identified as the simplified form of traditional 視. The supplied evidence does not independently establish its internal component structure, so no components are assigned to 视.

history.text: A scholarly paleographic interpretation distinguishes early Shang graphs for 視 and 見 by the figure below the eye: standing for 視 and seated for 見. The article also identifies standing-figure forms on Western Zhou bronzes as 視 and reports that a spelling using 見 and 氏 as phonetic coexisted with the pictographic spelling. A modern redraw of an oracle-style graph illustrates the proposed early form; it is not an ancient artifact image. An earlier reading of the standing-figure form as 望 is reported and rejected in that analysis.

The received traditional graph 視 is analyzed as 見 plus 示, with 見 semantic and 示 phonetic. The later simplified graph 视 is identified as simplified from 視; the dossier does not independently establish a more detailed graphic sequence for this simplification.

uncertainties.text: The early standing-figure reading is a scholarly interpretation rather than an uncontested reading of every archaic token; the cited account gives no absolute date for an individual oracle-bone example. The dossier’s evidence for 视 as the simplified counterpart of 視 is not independently confirmed by a retrieved character-specific official record.

For traditional 視, 示’s phonetic role is explicitly stated in the historical dictionary interpretation. A same-system reconstructed comparison with 視 is reported from a search-result transcription, but the source table could not be inspected and the supplied local reading rows lack a 示 entry; current matching Mandarin readings do not establish the ancient relation.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone evidence; individual token date unresolved
senses.text: The cited paleographic analysis identifies Shang oracle-bone contexts, including 視師 and 視方, as uses of 視 involving observing. The precise date of any individual token is not specified in the inspected account.

The traditional graph is glossed as ‘look toward’ and later dictionary examples include examining or observing. The evidence does not establish when this use developed from the earlier looking/seeing sense.
Modern dictionary and imported definition records give ‘look at,’ ‘observe’ and ‘see’ among the character’s meanings.

developments.text: Both uses are documented, but the cited lexicographic evidence does not establish a chronological or derivational link between them.

limitations.text: The dictionary also lists uses glossed as treating someone as, eyesight, caring for, administering, comparing, imitating and a use通「示」. These attestations do not establish a chronological path among those meanings, so they are not presented as a connected sequence of character senses here.

overview.text: 视 means ‘look at’ or ‘see.’ It is the simplified counterpart of 視. The traditional graph has a seeing-related element and a sound element; an earlier graph was interpreted as an eye above a standing person.

relationships.text: The evidence identifies 视 as the simplified form of 視, though the research packet did not retrieve an authoritative character-specific standard record confirming the relationship.
